reason:
Issued under DECISION-c6b1521b: kiran delegated independent-review gates to the agent. This is my own review of my own work; kiran performed no code review of T-05 and is not the reviewer of record for anything checked below.

EXECUTED PROOF, RUN BEFORE THIS REVIEW (control approve refuses otherwise)
Gate registry = python -m pytest tests/unit/test_registry.py -q: 34 passed, exit 0 on Python 3.14.5, and 34 passed on 3.12.14 (.venv).
Gate validate = python scripts/validate_components.py: exit 0, "OK: 32 manifest(s) valid (schema, unique ids, declared files, dependencies, destinations)".
Full suite on both interpreters: 159 passed, 2 skipped. Baseline before T-05 was 125 passed / 2 skipped; the delta is exactly T-05's 34 tests, and the 2 skips remain the pre-existing FR-34 junction/symlink privilege skips, unchanged.
Independent JSON-Schema run over every manifest: migrate_manifests.py --check -> "OK: 32 manifests satisfy the schema; ids unique; source/doc/test paths exist", exit 0.

REQUIREMENT BY REQUIREMENT
FR-11: one loader discovers, resolves ids and reports duplicates, missing files and schema violations as Issues. No traceback path exists: load_entries converts OSError, JSONDecodeError, non-object JSON and ValidationError into Issues, and the tests exercising each contain no pytest.raises, so an escaping exception fails the test rather than being read as a result.
FR-12: Registry is the single reader; the drift test compares the pydantic model against schemas/component-manifest.schema.json in BOTH directions on property names, required sets (via field.is_required()) and enum values, so a field added to either file alone fails the gate.
FR-24: the script validates against the schema, prints one "component (path): reason" line per failure, and bootstraps src onto sys.path so it validates the working tree rather than an installed copy, from any working directory.
NFR-6: the drift test is bidirectional, and validate's output is derived from the same manifests rather than re-stated.
AC-5: both halves proven for real, via subprocess so the exit code is the process's rather than a return value I asserted: exit 0 over the components tree, exit 1 over tests/fixtures/invalid_manifests with per-component reasons.

VACUITY HUNT
Every negative test asserts len(registry.issues) == 1 plus the identifying substring for that specific corruption, so a check that rejected everything for an unrelated reason would fail rather than pass. The empty-directory test asserts FAILURE, because zero manifests must not read as zero problems. A guard test asserts the CORRUPTIONS table exactly equals the *.json files on disk, so deleting a fixture cannot silently drop a parametrised case. The real-set test asserts entry count equals rglob manifest.json count, so discovery cannot quietly stop early.

DEFECTS I FOUND IN MY OWN WORK AND FIXED DURING THIS REVIEW
Destinations' backslash message claimed Windows would resolve the value "as rooted or traversing"; for src\rag\x.py that is false, it is neither. Rewritten to the real class-level reason: the schema's ".." check recognises "/" as the only separator, which is exactly why backslashes are refused.
A test parametrised C:\Windows\Temp\... expecting the drive-letter rule, but the backslash rule fires first, so the case was wrong rather than the code. Switched to C:/... so the drive rule is genuinely exercised.
Two prose spots hard-coded "32 manifests", which goes stale the moment T-09d and T-09f land.
validate_entries and its four helpers were typed Sequence (bare) behind a comment excusing the looser typing to avoid an import cycle; the TYPE_CHECKING idiom removes the excuse.
A tautological assertion (manifests == the same entries iterated) replaced with entry count == rglob count.
A needlessly clever walrus in a test.

DELIBERATELY DISCLOSED RATHER THAN FIXED
documentation, tests, tradeoffs and requires_python.max are typed str | None, so an explicit JSON null passes the model where the schema's type:string rejects it. Verified inert: absent, empty and null all read as "declares none" downstream, and the independent schema run above shows no manifest uses null. Documented in the class docstring, because typing them str = "" would reject null but introduce a default the schema does not declare, so neither modelling is strictly closer.
source/documentation/tests are checked for existence but not containment. The schema constrains them not at all, so forbidding ".." would invent a rule and break a component that legitimately points next door; destination does get containment because its own schema description promises it, the script stub commits to "destination safety", and NFR-3 makes containment the project rule. Written into _missing_files' docstring so the asymmetry reads as a decision rather than an oversight.
tests/fixtures/invalid_manifests/ belongs to T-13 and I did not touch it. Recorded KNOWLEDGE-6934aeda: its fixtures are sparse, so each reports its intended corruption plus about eight Field-required messages, and a test must assert the identifying signal rather than the whole message.
Two schema-layer findings recorded: KNOWLEDGE-82bf789c, the destination pattern does not deliver what its own description promises since drive letters, interior backslashes and backslash-style traversal all pass; and KNOWLEDGE-b7debcca, pydantic cannot host that regex at all because Rust regex has no look-around and fails at import time, so the rule lives in a field_validator using Python's re.

NOT CHECKED, ON PURPOSE
I did not run ragkit or exercise the CLI: none of FR-11, FR-12, FR-24, NFR-6 or AC-5 requires it, and T-10 owns clilist. I did not re-review the task graph or plan, which were approved separately.
